issues.description: getCategoryLabel heuristic silently produces wrong labels for known IDs (e.g., 'unused' -> 'Unuse', 'logging' -> 'Loggi').
issues.detail: The new heuristic lowercases the tail of words >3 chars and capitalizes only the first letter, but it also calls .slice(1).toLowerCase() — fine. However the rule 'short words = uppercase' misfires on legitimate non-acronyms, and the previous explicit CATEGORY_LABELS table was deleted. Without an invariant ('every known category ID maps to its canonical label'), regressions are silent. Reinstate the explicit table as the authoritative source; use heuristics only as fallback.

issues.description: HorizontalBarChart recomputes Math.max(...data.map(...)) inside the per-row render, turning an O(n) render into O(n^2).
issues.detail: maxValue is computed inside the .map callback for each row rather than hoisted above the loop. For small n this is harmless, but the invariant 'maxValue is constant across rows' should be expressed by hoisting it. This is the canonical 'optimize the loop bound, not the body' fix — and it also makes the code read correctly.

issues.description: SEVERITY_ORDER now has two keys mapping to value 4 ('Informational' and 'Info') with no comment stating the invariant.
issues.detail: Adding 'Info: 4' as an alias is reasonable, but the data structure now encodes 'multiple keys may share a rank' without saying so. A one-line literate comment ('aliases share rank; iteration order is not defined over aliases') would prevent a future reader from assuming uniqueness and breaking a downstream sort.

issues.description: CategorySelector conflates empty string and 'all' sentinel without stating why.
issues.detail: handleValueChange treats value === '' || value === 'all' as null. The Select can only emit 'all' or a real categoryId here, so the '' branch is dead code — or it guards against a contract the reader cannot see. Either drop the '' check or comment the invariant ('shadcn Select may emit '' on clear').

issues.description: displayPercentage and calculatedWidth duplicate the same fallback arithmetic with subtly different denominators.
issues.detail: calculatedWidth uses item.value/maxValue*100; displayPercentage uses item.value/total*100. Both fall back from item.percentage. The two quantities are semantically different (bar width vs. share-of-total) but the code does not say so. A two-line comment naming each quantity would make the function readable without running it.

review.summary: The PR is mostly straightforward UI plumbing, but the extraction of getCategoryLabel trades an explicit, auditable lookup table for a heuristic whose invariant ('known category IDs round-trip to canonical labels') is no longer stated or guaranteed — categories like 'unused', 'logging', 'storage' will be labeled correctly only by accident of the >3-char rule, and any future ID that breaks the pattern will silently mislabel. The horizontal bar chart fix is correct but recomputes the max inside the row loop; hoist it. Several new branches (CategorySelector sentinels, dual percentage computations) would benefit from one-line literate comments stating the invariant. Decision: UNDER-AUDITED on categories.ts, NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on the chart and selector, otherwise RIGOROUS.
